text:
incident-bot: P0 alert — elevated 5xx rate (avg ~12%) on /v1/generate in region us-west-2. Impact: hosted requests failing for some customers. Pager: #eng-oncall. Grafana: https://grafana.company/redwood/d/abc123. Please ACK and start triage.
Maya: ACKing, I'm primary oncall. grabbing initial triage.
Ravi: I'm secondary, standing by. ETA ~5m if needed.
Maya: Initial look — runtime pods showing OOMKill and connection resets. Errors spiked at 15:22 UTC. Suspect large batch from customer abc-corp triggering memory surge.
Jordan (runtime-oncall): @Maya I'm on it — pulling pod logs and KV cache stats for us-west-2-prod now.
Priya (infra-oncall): If nodes didn't scale, could be autoscaler/quota. Checking nodegroup provisioning and cloud quotas.
Sam (security): Any sign of auth abuse or anomalous IPs? I can run a quick correlation.
Liza (support): I'll draft an initial customer note once we have mitigation steps and ETA.
Maya: Quick mitigation plan: 1) apply temporary rate limit for offending tenant 2) scale runtime deployment +2 replicas 3) enable fallback/model-variant for hosted route. Execute in that order.
Ravi: Applying rate limit now:
```
redwood ctl rate-limit apply --tenant abc-corp --region us-west-2 --limit 5r/s --note "auto-mitigate P0"
```
Ravi: rate-limit applied, response looks OK.
Jordan: K8s scale started: `kubectl -n runtime scale deploy/runtime-prod --replicas=10` — rollout started (pod restarts happening).
Jordan: logs show OOMKilled on runtime-03 and some "too many open files" warnings. Collecting lsof output and /var/log/kern.log.
Priya: Node autoscaler attempted scale but hit quota limit on vCPU. Opening cloud quota increase ticket now (INC-7892). If provisioning delays > 5m, consider moving some traffic to us-west-1 standby.
Sam: Security scan shows no auth spikes or malformed requests — looks like resource exhaustion rather than attack.
Maya: Support note draft: "We're investigating elevated errors in us-west-2; mitigation underway. Expected recovery within 15-30m. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." Add phone contact?
Liza: Added phone contact. Sending out to affected customers in 10m unless we can close faster.
Maya: Oncall handoff/coverage: I'm primary until 16:00 UTC. Ravi is secondary. I may need to step out at 15:50 UTC for 10m — gap 16:00-16:20 UTC needs coverage; @Priya can you cover infra escalations then?
Ravi: I can provide primary coverage 16:00-16:20 if Maya must step out, but might still be handling infra pager. Priya, can you confirm?
Priya: I can be available 16:00-16:20 for infra escalations. If primary needed, ping me in thread and I'll take over.
Jordan: Runtime runbook ref: runbooks/runtime/oom-and-leaks.md — steps: check dmesg for OOM, lsof to find fd leaks, restart affected pods, check kvcache hit-rate, dump metrics to /tmp/incident-<ts>. Tar logs with `tar czf /tmp/oom-logs.tgz /var/log/pods/*`.
Maya: Routing question for clarity: If problem persists after scaling and rate-limiting, do we escalate to Infra or keep in Runtime team? My call: runtime-first (process-level), escalate to infra for node/quota/network issues. Security if we detect abnormal auth/traffic patterns. Support handles comms. Agree?
Priya: Agreed. Infra only if node provisioning/quota or networking prevents scaling or causes pod churn.
Sam: Agreed on security escalation boundaries.
Jordan: Update: new replicas ready, KV cache warming. 5xx rate dropping to ~2% over last 3 minutes. Monitoring for regression.
Maya: Nice. I'll keep monitoring for another 15m. If stable, we'll move to postmortem/RCAs.
incident-bot: Incident update: status=mitigating; severity=P0; owners=[Maya,Ravi,Jordan,Priya]; first_alert=3023456789; next_checkin=3023457370.
Maya: Closing loop: if anyone picks this up after 16:20 UTC, first check node quota and pod OOM history. Thanks all for quick responses :heart:
